messages:
Lena Morales: Acme Global procurement just dropped a PO but says invoice MUST read 'Acme Global, Inc'. They will only accept marketplace purchases. Can we get AWS invoice to show parent name?
Samir Khan: Short answer: AWS invoices show the marketplace seller and usually the buyer account. If their marketplace account isn't under the parent legal entity, that's a mismatch.
Lena Morales: They said their AWS credits live at the consolidated corporate account, so they want charges applied there.
Jordan Lee (Deal Desk): Options: 1) buyer adds billing alias/linked account so AWS invoice matches parent, 2) we issue a supplemental commercial invoice on our letterhead that ties the AWS invoice to the PO, 3) convert to Dedicated and invoice directly (affects pricing).
Priya Desai (Finance): Prefers #2 as low lift for us, but we need written acceptance from procurement acknowledging AWS invoice remains the legal tax invoice. Also need EIN and billing address. Manual invoice process will add ~1 week to payout.
procurement-bot: Private Offer SKU: rwd-market-PO-98765. Reminder: AWS fee deduction still applies even with supplemental invoice.
Lena Morales: Procurement refuses addendum language earlier; they said only an exact match on invoice header will clear AP.
Samir Khan: If they refuse any supplemental doc, deal desk can approve a one-off exception — we can provide a custom invoice to Acme Global that mirrors the marketplace charges, but legal must sign off. This is manual and tracked as an exception.
Jordan Lee (Deal Desk): Drafting exception language now. Also note: if customer uses AWS credits, the supplemental invoice must show net $0 if credits cover it, otherwise AP will be confused.
Priya Desai (Finance): Action for Lena: get the PO header lines: legal name, tax ID, billing address, and confirm whether they require line-item breakout of marketplace fees. I need that to assess revenue recognition and payout reconciliation.
Lena Morales: Sent back their PO details in chat: PO#: ACME-PO-2026-411, Name: Acme Global, Inc; EIN: 12-3456789; Addr: 123 Corporate Way, Suite 400. They still say no addendum, only exact invoice.
Jordan Lee (Deal Desk): I put together this template wording: 
``` 
Redwood Inference, Inc. will provide a supplemental commercial invoice to Acme Global, Inc. to assist in reconciliation. The Amazon.com, Inc. marketplace invoice remains the legal tax invoice. Redwood will not seek duplicate payment for amounts invoiced by AWS. Private Offer ID: rwd-market-PO-98765.
```
Priya Desai (Finance): Good. Add: "Supplier contact for remittance questions: Priya Desai, finance@redwood.com" and a clause about credits: "If buyer's AWS credits fully cover charges, the supplemental invoice will reflect $0 due."
Lena Morales: Procurement replied: they'll accept the supplemental invoice only if it's on company letterhead and includes the Private Offer ID and a contact. They asked for a signed PDF before processing the PO.
Samir Khan: Legal signoff needed but low risk. Deal desk: mark as exception and attach to opportunity.
Jordan Lee (Deal Desk): Approved pending legal. I created CRM flag EXC-BILLING-ACME.
Priya Desai (Finance): Timeline: 5 business days to generate and sign supplemental invoice + 2 days for AP to confirm. Expect 7-10 day payout delta. I'll own remittance Qs.
Lena Morales: Thanks. Ill update the buyer and attach the signed supplemental invoice on letterhead once legal clears. :white_check_mark:
procurement-bot: Ticket created: BILL-4872 (manual-supplemental-invoice-acme)
